content:
Hey everyone! 👋
 As a second-year law student catching up on the morning newspaper I’ve been thinking a lot about a major issue happening right now about how technology and critical minerals are being turned into tools of conflict and crime.
 Normally, we talk about tech and critical minerals (like the rare earth metals used in phones, laptops and electric cars) as amazing things for green energy and innovation. But lately, countries and bad actors are starting to use them as weapons to control global trade.
 Reading through the news a few things really stand out from a legal perspective which are 
 Supply Chain Choke points -  When a few countries control all the critical minerals, they can easily cut off supplies or hike prices, throwing global manufacturing into chaos.
 Illegal Trade & Crime - Beyond government politics, weak rules mean these valuable resources often end up tied to illegal mining, money laundering, and black-market syndicates.
 It is wild to see how fast modern laws and international agreements have to adapt to deal with these new challenges !
 How do you think we can keep global supply chains fair and safe from being controlled or weaponized? Let’s talk about it in the comments! 👇
​#Geopolitics #Critical minerals #International law #Supply chains #Tech policy #Global trade
